key_insight: The paper provides an exact and scalable shape-differentiation framework for multi-phase topology optimisation on unfitted finite elements, enabling reliable optimization of complex multi-material and multi-physics systems.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational mechanics engineers a practical way to optimize structures with multiple phases and irregular boundaries without relying on fitted meshes, which is important for realistic design problems in diffusion, elasticity, and FSI.
method: Derive exact discrete shape-calculus expressions for multi-phase systems using convex geometry.
Build an open-source automatic shape differentiation framework on polytopal cutting and multiple level-set functions.
Apply the framework to anisotropic diffusion, linear elasticity, and fluid–structure interaction.
evidence_signal: The framework matches exact expressions to near machine precision, agrees with finite differences, and shows near-ideal weak scaling up to 1.65 billion finite elements on 13,824 cores.
watch_item: The method depends on a specialized unfitted/discrete geometry pipeline, so robustness and setup complexity may be a concern for highly intricate interfaces or new solver stacks.
paper_title: Shape calculus and automatic differentiation for multi-phase level-set topology optimisation with unfitted finite elements
